title: Picking a layer brings its row into view
goal: Click something on the picture and the layers list does not move, so the row for what you just picked can be sitting off the bottom of a long list with no sign of it. The list should bring the picked row into view, so what you have in your hand and what the list is showing are never two different things.
notes:
Reported by the user on 2026-09-13: "when a single layer is clicked on, the layers list doesn't scroll to the selected layer".

Confirmed by reading: there is no scroll-to-row machinery in the layers list at all. Sources/Photonz/LayersListView.swift:279 is the ScrollView and :404 the LazyVStack of rows, and a grep for scrollTo, ScrollViewReader, scrollPosition or anything like them across that file finds nothing. So this is missing rather than broken.

The trap: the list is deliberately lazy. The comment at LayersListView.swift:366 says "LazyVStack builds a row the first time it comes into view", and :198 and :257 carry logic about which rows are built and a reserved row count, added by the shipped task 'the-layers-list-only-builds-the-rows-you-can-see'. Scrolling to a row that has never been built is exactly the case that quietly does nothing, and it is also the case this report is about, because the row the user could not see is by definition off screen. Test with a list long enough that the target has never been realised, not with a list of six.

Do not let this fight the work already queued about the panel moving itself. The pending task 'picking-a-text-layer-leaves-its-settings-below-t' (p2, seq 10) is about the PROPERTIES panel scrolling to a picked thing's settings, and it is waiting on a user decision about whether picking something should move the panel at all. That is a different surface from the layers list, but it is the same question asked twice, and one of its acceptance items already says "Clicking a row in the layers list does not scroll that list off the top of the panel". Read that task and its decision card first; if the user answers that picking should never move anything, this task has to be revisited rather than built as written. Say in the log which way it went.

The "already visible does nothing" item is the one that decides whether this feels good or annoying. A list that re-scrolls on every pick, including picks of rows you can already see, is worse than one that never scrolls.
acceptance: Picking a layer on the canvas scrolls the layers list so that layer's row is visible
A row that is ALREADY visible does not move the list at all, so picking things near the top does not jolt the panel
The list moves as little as it has to rather than centring the row, and the movement is animated rather than jumping
A layer inside a collapsed group opens that group so its row can actually be shown, rather than scrolling to where the row would have been
Picking several layers brings the one you just clicked into view rather than guessing among them
It works the same for a layer picked any other way: the arrow keys, Select All, undo restoring a selection, and a newly drawn shape
Scrolling the list by hand and then clicking the same layer again does not fight you
A playtest walk picks a layer far down a long list and checks its row is on screen afterwards
Audit under queue/audits/ with a long list before and after, and anything rough filed as a follow-up

log.note: READ THE OTHER TASK FIRST, as the notes asked. The decision on 'picking-a-text-layer-leaves-its-settings-below-t' resolved on 2026-09-13 as "What you picked sits at the top" — the user chose REORDERING the properties panel over SCROLLING it. That is a decision about the panel's sections, not about the layers list: a list cannot reorder its rows to put the picked one first, and the user filed this task the same day, after answering that card. So it was built as written. The one thing carried across from that answer is the taste it shows: it does not move if it does not have to.

ADVERSARIAL REVIEW, before building. (a) The shortest version is the whole version: there is no new control, no new affordance and nothing to learn, so the only risk is moving when it should not. Every rule here is a rule about NOT moving. (b) The collision that matters is the band: a rubber band on the canvas rewrites the multi-selection on every frame, and a list that chased it would be a list scrolling under your pointer sixty times a second. Answered by testing the WHOLE arriving selection for visibility, so once anything it caught is on screen nothing moves; measured in the walk, a band round eighteen layers moved the list 40pt, once. (c) Dragging a row to reorder cannot fight it either: the row you grabbed is by definition on screen. (d) Two of the pick paths the acceptance names do not exist in the app — the arrow keys nudge the picked layer rather than stepping to the next one, and Command A marquees the canvas rather than selecting every layer — so those clauses are met by every path that DOES move the selection going through one place.

BUILT. Core: LayerListMetrics.rowTop / revealOffset (PhotonzCore, pure, nine tests in LayerListRevealTests) works out the offset from the row's PLACE rather than from its frame, which is the trap the task notes named: the row this feature is about is one the lazy stack has never built, and an unbuilt row has no frame. It reuses DockReveal for the shortest-move rule, so the layers list and the properties panel now decide 'is it on screen' the same way. App: EditorState.layersListReveal is the ask (ids + a tick, so the same layer asked for twice reads as two asks), set by revealInLayersList, which every selection path already funnelled through; LayersListView applies it with ScrollPosition.scrollTo(y:) inside a 0.24s easeInOut. Scroll offset is kept in a plain box (LayerListScroll), never in @State, so a scroll does not redraw the list.

FLAGGED next-layers-follow-pick, next only, on by default. LayersListView is shared between the releases, so only the SCROLL is behind the flag; opening the groups above a picked layer is what both releases already did.

VERIFIED on the probe with Screen Recording granted. New walk Scripts/playtest/layers-list-follows-pick-walk.json, 21 layers in a list showing five: picking the bottom-left rectangle scrolled 0 -> 598pt and its row is on screen; a row already on screen moved nothing; scrolled to the top by hand then clicking the same layer again moved nothing; a new shape brought the list back up 598 -> 0; stepping into a SHUT group opened it and scrolled to the piece (row 21); a band round eighteen layers moved 760 -> 720. New waitFor condition layerRowInView, plus layerRowsInView and layerReveal in every panel read.

ONE WALK NEEDED FIXING and it is worth knowing why: separate-into-layers-walk read rows that were no longer BUILT. It picks the Background row, which is the last one, so the list now scrolls to the bottom and the lazy stack lets go of the rows at the top; `expect` reads what the panel has built. Fixed by scrolling back up before the two claims, which also makes 'there is no Text 10' mean something, since a new layer would land at the top where it was not even looking. Any other walk that picks one layer and then claims a distant row is built could hit the same thing, which is why a sweep was asked for.

Scripts/test.sh green (6398 tests). layers-* walks, panel-controls-walk and open-groups-remembered-walk all pass. dock-picked-first-walk and contents-for-several-walk fail, both already failing in the 2026-09-14T03:26Z sweep before this change. A sweep was requested rather than run.

The layers list now follows what you pick: LayerListMetrics.revealOffset (PhotonzCore, 9 tests) plus EditorState.layersListReveal and LayersListView, flagged next-layers-follow-pick, Next only, on by default. A row already on screen never moves the list, the move is the shortest that shows the whole row, and a shut group opens first. Verified on the probe with real captures: new layers-list-follows-pick-walk covers the far row, the already-visible row, a hand scroll, a new shape, a shut group and a band. Scripts/test.sh green (6398). Audit at queue/audits/2026-09-13-layers-follow-pick.json; sweep requested because the change moves which rows the lazy stack has built (separate-into-layers-walk needed a scroll step).
